title: ～つもりだった — “I had intended to ～ (but…)”
summary: Past form of ～つもりだ. It says what you had planned or believed at some past point, usually followed by a result that went differently. It attaches to the dictionary form (plan) or the ta-form (a belief about what you did).

patterns.form: 動詞辞書形＋つもりだった
patterns.gloss: I had planned to do ～ (the plan did not happen)

patterns.form: 動詞た形／ない形＋つもりだった
patterns.gloss: I thought I had done ～ (but I hadn't, or it was wrong)

body.p: With the dictionary form, 行くつもりだった means “I had planned to go.” With the ta-form, 確認したつもりだった means “I believed I had checked.” In both cases the speaker knows now that reality was different.
It is normally followed by a contrast such as が, のに or けど, then the real result: 行くつもりだったが、行けなかった. Without any follow-up it can sound unfinished.
～つもりだ states a present plan (明日行くつもりだ). ～つもりだった looks back at a plan or belief that is now over or turned out wrong.

examples.ja: 行（い）くつもりだったが、用事（ようじ）ができて行（い）けなかった。
examples.romaji: Iku tsumori datta ga, youji ga dekite ikenakatta.
examples.tr: I had intended to go, but something came up and I couldn’t.
examples.note: Dictionary form + つもりだった = a plan that fell through.

examples.ja: 早（はや）く寝（ね）るつもりだったのに、気（き）づけば真夜中（まよなか）だった。
examples.romaji: Hayaku neru tsumori datta noni, kizukeba mayonaka datta.
examples.tr: I had intended to sleep early, but before I knew it, it was midnight.
examples.note: のに adds a feeling of regret or surprise.

examples.ja: きちんと確認（かくにん）したつもりだったが、間違（まちが）いがあった。
examples.romaji: Kichinto kakunin shita tsumori datta ga, machigai ga atta.
examples.tr: I thought I had checked it properly, but there was a mistake.
examples.note: Ta-form + つもりだった = a belief that proved wrong.

pitfalls: Do not use it for a plan that was carried out as planned. It implies that reality differed from the intention.
Dictionary form means “planned to”; ta-form means “believed I had”. Mixing them up changes the meaning completely.
